newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT- NYMEX OIL MUST HOLD SUPPORTS TO MOVE UP.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT- NYMEX OIL MUST HOLD SUPPORTS TO MOVE UP.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* NYMEX crude holds a steady uptrend and looks oversold, so anticipate some short covering ahead of the weekend.
* Heating oil is expected to remain stable with oversold RSI's keeping the technical downside limited. Gasoline may face a reversal of the one month uptrend if it closes below 64.40.

NYMEX crude and products weakness is seen short term on Friday. But analysts say certain key support levels must be held, particularly for gasoline, if the recent steady uptrend across the complex is to be held.
Short term momentum indicators for both crude and products have slipped into the oversold zone.
These combined, with the anticipated resultant short covering ahead of the weekend, are likely to provide the base for the markets to move higher again in the longer term.
GNI Research said in their daily report, "The short term indicators obviously take a bashing when prices make a reasonable down move as they have in the past two days."
They said the problems for crude were accentuated as gasoline went through a number of stops.

"Now the primary trend on the continuous daily (NYMEX crude) chart is at risk, September crude is already near to testing $20 in ACCESS trade and if gasoline gets hosed again crude will fall below this level."

Countering this Tom James at Credit Lyonnais Rouse in Singapore said, "(NYMEX crude) is still holding steady uptrend and looking technically oversold so anticipate some short covering ahead of the weekend"
On the spot month continuation chart for crude there is still some support around $19.95 stemming from July 23's $19.40 low if $20 goes.

Short term (10-day) moving averages have moved above the 70 percent level flagging the prompt weakness, but longer term (20-day) measures continue to show the market holding in steady uptrend stemming from June 30.
Heating oil completed and held a perfect 50 percent Fibonacci retracement yesterday with a low of 55.20 on the prompt contract.
"Today a close above this level and the moving average trend system level 55.30 will make yesterday's large drop a mere correction," James said.
He said he expected the heating oil market to remain stable with oversold RSI's keeping the technical downside limited.
Of gasoline James said, "The market broke key support on Thursday which may lead to a potential reversal of the one month uptrend if we close below 64.40 cents again today."
